note: Generated by `go test ./internal/compose/ -run TestTheAgentToolBudgetIsPublished -update-agent-tool-budget`; do not edit by hand. It reports what each scheduled agent's step costs the window it runs in before its transcript: the frame, the tool listing and the step schema. No run is offered the whole served catalog. Token counts use the ~4-bytes-per-token estimate the window itself uses, over what the runner's own renderer produces (runner.FixedStepCost). tool_cost rows do not add up to catalog.tokens: each is one tool rendered alone and divided by four, so every row carries its own rounding, while catalog.tokens divides the whole rendered listing once.

held_by.refuses: an agent_loop site declaring no tools, or tools on any other kind of site
a job carrying no allowlist, before any model call
an agent attaching every served tool, a tool this build does not serve, or one twice
a runner.Job anywhere in compose whose Tools is not an entry's own allowlist
an agent withholding nothing its scopes admit
an agent whose listing outgrows its share of the window

agents.name: morning_brief
agents.goal: Prepare the existing Morning Brief of the user this run acts for. First call read_brief. Its items are the queue already ranked for them; do not assemble a workspace-wide list. Read every record an item cites in its evidence_ids, its activities as well as its deal, then call annotate_brief ONCE, with one concise narrative and a grounded finding for every item in that same call: why it matters, what changed and the next move. An item with a previous_rank was already on this queue on the run's previous_local_day: say what has changed since then rather than reporting it as new. An item without one may simply not have ranked that day, so do not call it new either. Use each returned item_id unchanged, never its deal_id, and cite only that item's evidence_ids. Keep the existing order. If there are no items, finish without inventing a brief. A tool refusal means the findings were not saved: correct it before claiming completion.

agents.name: overnight_at_risk_sweep
agents.goal: Sweep the open deals your member owns for risk: deals with no activity in 14+ days, stakeholders gone quiet, or missing next steps. First call whats_slipping_this_week: in this run it returns only the at-risk deals your member owns. Each other member's run sweeps that member's deals, and a deal whose owner has not granted this sweep is swept by nobody, so do not read or log on a deal outside that list. A deal the retrieved context mentions is one example, not the sweep, so do not read or log on it before that list. Then read each listed deal, call catch_me_up_on on it and read_record each recent touch it lists, and log ONE note activity per at-risk deal, linked to that deal (links: [{entity_type: deal, entity_id: <its deal_id>}]). Its subject names the risk in a few words; its body states the finding and the evidence (cite the records you read). A note without a body is refused. Do not advance stages, send anything, or archive anything.
